s: A company's central IT team operates an organization in AWS Organizations for 12 subsidiaries, each with its own set of accounts. Savings Plans and volume discounts are purchased and kept centrally. The company wants each subsidiary to see a monthly bill and a cost and usage report calculated at public On-Demand rates plus a 4% central support fee, without seeing the organization's discounted rates. Each subsidiary must be able to view this data from its own accounts. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: Create a Cost Category for each subsidiary and give subsidiary users read-only access to AWS Cost Explorer in the management account.
Turn off Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discount sharing for the subsidiary accounts so that their bills show On-Demand rates.

Use AWS Billing Conductor to create a billing group for each subsidiary with a pricing plan that applies a 4% markup pricing rule, and configure pro forma Cost and Usage Reports for each billing group.
Create a CUR 2.0 export, and use an AWS Lambda function with the AWS Price List API to recalculate each line at public prices plus 4% and write the results to each subsidiary's S3 bucket.

w.y: AWS Billing Conductor creates pro forma billing data per billing group using a pricing plan, so each subsidiary sees public On-Demand rates plus a 4% markup instead of the organization's discounted rates. Pro forma Cost and Usage Reports and console views are available to each billing group, with no custom pipeline, giving the LEAST operational overhead.

o.A: Shows actual discounted costs, cannot add a markup, and grants access to the management account.
o.B: Changes the real bill and raises the organization's total cost, and still provides no 4% fee.
o.C: Correct: managed showback at custom rates without exposing actual discounts.
o.D: Custom recalculation code must be built and maintained.

d: LEAST operational overhead; without seeing the organization's discounted rates
